hits.full_text:
An influencer is incentivized by attention, so their content must be optimized to be consumed and forgotten (cheap dopamine).

A personal brand is incentivized by money, so their content must be optimized to move you down their sales funnel.

An artisan is incentivized by the satisfaction that comes from the quality of their work. They need attention and money, but for the sole purpose of spending more time on work they enjoy and the impact it has.

Become an artisan.
hits.hook: Dan Koe: influencer vs personal brand vs artisan, 'become an artisan' (~51k views, 116 replies)

patterns: November 1 brought a flood of near-identical 'new month, fresh start' posts, many copied word for word across accounts. They get likes but almost no conversation, so a specific, small version of the fresh start stands out.
The clocks went back overnight, and people are talking about the dark at 5 and seasonal depression. Questions that ask how it actually feels get replies; reminder posts don't.
Paper versus apps keeps coming up: a paper planner replacing 340 overdue tasks, notebook-buying jokes from neurodivergent accounts, glass pens for letters.
Reading posts are first-time classics (Wuthering Heights) and October wrap-ups, and the AO3 outage is still pushing fanfic readers to finish whole books.
#buildinpublic is tired of itself. The posts with life in them share honest tiny numbers or what got cut, not MRR screenshots.
On the watchlist, Visakan's parenting link (~337k) and Dan Koe's 'become an artisan' (~51k) lead; both reward craft and care over attention.

reply_ideas.description: switched to a paper planner because their to-do app had 340 overdue tasks haunting them
reply_ideas.reply_text: What I like about paper is that nothing rolls over on its own. If a task wants to come with you to the next page, you have to write it out again by hand, and a lot of them don't survive that. Did any of the 340 make the cut?

reply_ideas.description: a joke that notebook companies are pyramid schemes for autistic and ADHD people, since everyone talks three friends into buying one
reply_ideas.reply_text: I think the real product is the first page. Most of the journals on anyone's shelf are blank after page twelve, and we still buy the next one. Which part got you this year, the paper or the cover?

reply_ideas.description: a small business owner asking why people assume you don't know what you're doing just because your following is still small
reply_ideas.reply_text: I think a small following looks like inexperience to people who have never started anything from zero. Every account they admire had a stretch where almost nobody was watching. What do you make? I'd rather hear about the work than the follower count.

video_tip: 15 seconds, no face. Split screen: on one side a phone screen fills with overdue-task alerts, on the other a hand copies a short list onto a fresh cream page with a fountain pen and leaves a few tasks off. Pen sounds only. End on a card that reads 'What made the cut?' Pairs with the paper post.

x_posts.title: Smallest start
x_posts.text:
Half my feed is fresh-start posts for November. I trust a small start more than a big one, the kind that's almost too small to count, like one line in a notebook before bed.

What's the smallest thing you're starting this month?
x_posts.why: November fresh-start flood; a specific small version stands out

x_posts.title: Arizona clocks
x_posts.text:
Everyone's talking about the clocks going back, and here in Arizona we never change them. It still gets dark earlier every week.

Is it the time change that gets to you, or is it the dark?
x_posts.why: clocks went back overnight, dark at 5, seasonal depression talk

x_posts.title: Worth the ink
x_posts.text:
A to-do app will carry every unfinished task forward forever. Paper makes you copy it out by hand, and a lot of tasks don't look worth the ink by the next morning.

Has anyone else gone back to paper for that reason?
x_posts.why: paper planner vs 340 overdue tasks, notebook jokes
